questions.text: A solid metallic cone of base radius 14 cm and height 7 cm is melted and recast into a solid sphere. Taking π = 22/7, what is the surface area of the sphere?
questions.explanation: Cone volume = ⅓π × 14² × 7 = 1,372π/3. Sphere: 4/3 πR³ = 1,372π/3, so R³ = 343 and R = 7 cm. Surface area = 4πR² = 4 × 22/7 × 49 = 616 cm².
questions.trap: Using the diameter in place of the radius.
questions.revise: Recasting: equate volumes, then find the new dimension
wrongReasons: Used the sphere's radius as 3.5 cm
Used the diameter as the radius

questions.text: The slant height of a right circular cone is 25 cm and its curved surface area is 550 cm². Taking π = 22/7, what is its volume?
questions.explanation: Curved area πrl = 550 gives r = 550 × 7 ÷ (22 × 25) = 7 cm. Height = √(25² − 7²) = 24 cm. Volume = ⅓ × 22/7 × 49 × 24 = 1,232 cm³.
questions.trap: Using the slant height as the height.
questions.revise: Cone: curved area to radius, then Pythagoras for height
wrongReasons: Used the slant height in place of the vertical height
Left out the ⅓ in the volume formula
Used half the radius in the volume

questions.text: Water flows through a circular pipe of internal diameter 14 cm at 10 km/h into a rectangular tank 11 m long and 7 m wide. Taking π = 22/7, how long will it take to raise the water level in the tank by 1.4 m?
questions.explanation: Flow per hour = π(0.07)² × 10,000 m = 154 m³. Volume needed = 11 × 7 × 1.4 = 107.8 m³. Time = 107.8 ÷ 154 = 0.7 hour = 42 minutes.
questions.trap: Mixing cm and m in the pipe's cross-section.
wrongReasons: Used half of the actual speed
Used the diameter as the radius
Used half of the rise in level

questions.text: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 32 cm. What is the distance between a pair of its opposite sides?
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × 24 × 32 = 384 cm². Side = √(12² + 16²) = 20 cm. Distance between opposite sides = area ÷ side = 384 ÷ 20 = 19.2 cm.
questions.trap: Giving the side as the answer.

questions.text: The parallel sides of an isosceles trapezium are 25 cm and 9 cm and each of its non-parallel sides is 17 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Half the difference of the parallel sides = (25 − 9)/2 = 8. Height = √(17² − 8²) = 15 cm. Area = ½ × (25 + 9) × 15 = 255 cm².
questions.trap: Using the slanting side as the height.
wrongReasons: Used the slant side 17 as the height
Used the longer parallel side as the average
Left out the ½ in the formula

questions.text: Four circles, each of radius 7 cm, touch one another so that their centres form a square. Taking π = 22/7, what is the area of the region enclosed between the four circles?
questions.explanation: The centres form a square of side 14 cm, area 196 cm². Each corner has a quarter circle of radius 7 inside the square; the four together equal one circle = 154 cm². Region = 196 − 154 = 42 cm².
questions.trap: Forgetting that four quarter-circles make one full circle.
wrongReasons: Gave the area of one circle
Gave the area of the square joining the centres

questions.text: A sector of angle 120° is cut from a circle of radius 21 cm and its straight edges are joined to form a cone. Taking π = 22/7, what is the total surface area of the cone?
questions.explanation: The sector's area becomes the curved surface: ⅓ × π × 21² = 462 cm². Arc length = ⅓ × 2π × 21 = 2πr, so r = 7 cm. Base area = π × 49 = 154. Total = 462 + 154 = 616 cm².
questions.trap: Giving only the curved surface or forgetting the base.
questions.revise: Sector to cone: slant = sector radius, base circumference = arc
wrongReasons: Gave only the curved surface area
Gave the area of the full circle

questions.text: The median of the following distribution is 28. Find the missing frequency x.
questions.explanation: N = 38 + x. The median class is 20–30 with cumulative frequency 16 before it. 28 = 20 + [(N/2 − 16)/x] × 10, so (N/2 − 16) = 0.8x, i.e. 19 + 0.5x − 16 = 0.8x, so 0.3x = 3 and x = 10.
questions.trap: Using N instead of N/2.
questions.revise: Median formula with an unknown frequency
wrongReasons: Used the wrong cumulative frequency before the median class
Used the frequency of the next class
Took the frequency of the class after the median class

questions.text: What is the mean of the distribution given in the table?
questions.trap: Using upper limits or the unweighted mean.
wrongReasons: Took the mean of the class marks without weights
Rounded using the median class mark
Used the upper class limits in place of class marks

questions.text: By what percent is the average marks of the four students in Mathematics more than their average marks in English?
questions.explanation: Mathematics total = 72 + 81 + 56 + 91 = 300, average 75. English total = 50 + 60 + 70 + 60 = 240, average 60. Percent more = (75 − 60)/60 × 100 = 25%.
questions.trap: Dividing by the wrong base.
questions.revise: Percent change uses the base of comparison
wrongReasons: Divided the difference by the Mathematics average instead of the English average
Gave the difference of the averages
Mixed up the base and the comparison

questions.text: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when one person weighing 65 kg is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Total weight rises by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg, so the new person weighs 65 + 20 = 85 kg.
questions.trap: Adding only the change in the average.
questions.revise: Replacement: change in total = n × change in mean
wrongReasons: Added 2.5 to the old weight only

questions.text: What is the standard deviation of the seven consecutive even numbers 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22 and 24?
questions.explanation: For 7 consecutive integers, variance = (7² − 1)/12 = 4, SD = 2. Consecutive even numbers are twice the integers, so the SD doubles to 4. Check: mean 18, deviations ±6, ±4, ±2, 0, variance = 2(36 + 16 + 4)/7 = 16, SD = 4.
questions.trap: Giving the SD of consecutive integers.
questions.revise: SD scales with the common difference
wrongReasons: This is the SD of seven consecutive integers
Gave the range of the middle terms
Took the variance of integers as 8

questions.text: The mean of 100 observations was calculated as 50. It was later found that 84 had been recorded as 48 and 55 as 76. What is the correct mean?
questions.trap: Reversing the sign of a correction.
wrongReasons: Applied the corrections with the wrong sign

questions.text: What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 for 1½ years at 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.trap: Using the annual rate with half-yearly periods.
questions.revise: CI: halve the rate, double the periods
wrongReasons: Used simple interest for the period
Compounded annually for one year, then took simple interest for the half-year

questions.text: A starts a business with ₹36,000. After 4 months B joins with ₹45,000, and 3 months after that C joins with ₹60,000. At the end of the year the total profit is ₹91,000. What is C's share?
questions.trap: Using the wrong number of months for C.
wrongReasons: Counted C's capital for only 4 months

questions.text: A train crosses a pole in 12 seconds and a platform 300 m long in 27 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Let the length be L m. L/12 = (L + 300)/27, so 27L = 12L + 3,600 and L = 240 m. Speed = 240/12 = 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.
questions.trap: Not converting m/s to km/h.
wrongReasons: Gave the speed in m/s as if it were km/h
Used a platform crossing time of 24 seconds

questions.text: A vessel contains milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3. When 20 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water, the ratio becomes 7 : 8. What was the quantity of the mixture initially?
questions.explanation: Let the mixture be T litres. Milk left = 7/10 × (T − 20). Final milk fraction = 7/15. So 0.7(T − 20) = 7T/15, i.e. 0.7T − 14 = 0.4667T, giving T = 60 litres. Check: milk 42 → 28; water 18 → 12 + 20 = 32; 28 : 32 = 7 : 8.
questions.trap: Treating the 20 litres removed as pure milk.
questions.revise: Replacement: removed mixture carries both components
wrongReasons: Ignored that the removed mixture contains milk
Took the total after adding 20 litres
Used the ratio 7 : 3 as 7 : 8 for the final quantity

questions.subtopic: Gain and loss on two articles
questions.text: A trader sells two articles at ₹1,980 each, gaining 10% on one and losing 10% on the other. What is the net loss in rupees?
questions.explanation: Cost of the first = 1,980/1.1 = 1,800; cost of the second = 1,980/0.9 = 2,200. Total cost = 4,000, total selling price = 3,960. Loss = ₹40.
questions.trap: Assuming equal percentages cancel.
questions.revise: Equal gain % and loss % on equal SP always means a loss
wrongReasons: Assumed the equal gain and loss cancel

questions.text: In triangle ABC, ∠A = 90° and AD is perpendicular to BC, with BD = 9 cm and DC = 16 cm. What is the area of triangle ABC?
questions.explanation: AD² = BD × DC = 144, so AD = 12 cm. BC = 25 cm. Area = ½ × 25 × 12 = 150 cm².
questions.trap: Giving AD² instead of the area.
questions.revise: Right triangle: altitude² = product of the segments
wrongReasons: Left out the ½ in the area formula
Gave the square of the altitude

questions.text: In triangle ABC, I is the incentre and O is the circumcentre. If ∠A = 52°, what is the difference between ∠BIC and ∠BOC?
questions.trap: Using the wrong formula for ∠BOC.
questions.revise: Angles at the incentre and circumcentre

questions.text: From an external point P, a tangent PT of length 12 cm and a secant PAB are drawn, with PA = 8 cm. What is the length of the chord AB?
questions.explanation: PT² = PA × PB, so 144 = 8 × PB and PB = 18 cm. AB = PB − PA = 18 − 8 = 10 cm.
questions.trap: Giving PB instead of AB.

questions.text: The tangent at a point T of a circle with centre O and a chord TQ make an angle of 62°. What is the angle subtended by the chord TQ at the centre O?
questions.explanation: The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment, so the angle at the circumference is 62°. The angle at the centre is double: 124°.
steps: Tangent-chord angle = angle in the alternate segment = 62°
questions.trap: Stopping at the angle at the circumference.
wrongReasons: Gave half of the tangent-chord angle

questions.subtopic: Sum of cubes with sin and cos
questions.text: If sin θ + cos θ = 7/5, what is the value of sin³θ + cos³θ?
questions.explanation: Squaring: 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ = 49/25, so sin θ cos θ = 12/25. sin³θ + cos³θ = (sin θ + cos θ)(1 − sin θ cos θ) = (7/5)(13/25) = 91/125 = 0.728.
questions.trap: Using sin θ cos θ = 24/25.

questions.text: A flagpole stands on top of a tower. From a point on the ground 40 m from the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 45° and the tangent of the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 3/4. What is the length of the flagpole?
questions.explanation: Total height = 40 × tan 45° = 40 m. Tower = 40 × 3/4 = 30 m. Flagpole = 40 − 30 = 10 m.
questions.trap: Giving the tower or total height.
questions.revise: Heights and distances with two angles
wrongReasons: Gave the height of the tower
Gave the total height of tower and pole

questions.text: If sec θ = 5/4 and θ is acute, what is the value of cos θ/(1 − sin θ) + cos θ/(1 + sin θ)?
questions.explanation: The expression = cos θ[(1 + sin θ) + (1 − sin θ)]/(1 − sin²θ) = 2 cos θ/cos²θ = 2 sec θ = 2 × 5/4 = 2.5.
steps: Expression = 2 cos θ / cos²θ = 2 sec θ
questions.trap: Simplifying to 2 cos θ.
wrongReasons: Took the value of 2 cos θ

questions.trap: Using the wrong sign in the cube identity.

questions.text: If α and β are the roots of x² − 6x + 4 = 0, what is the value of α³ + β³?
questions.trap: Adding instead of subtracting the correction term.

questions.text: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 56 years. Eight years ago the father was seven times as old as the son. What will be the father's age after 5 years?
questions.explanation: Let the son be S. Father = 56 − S. 56 − S − 8 = 7(S − 8), so 48 − S = 7S − 56, 8S = 104 and S = 13. Father = 43. After 5 years = 48.
questions.trap: Giving the present age.
questions.revise: Age problems: set up the earlier-year equation

questions.text: How many trailing zeros are there in 125! (the factorial of 125)?
questions.trap: Counting only the multiples of 5.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of 13⁵⁷ × 17²³?
questions.explanation: 13⁵⁷ ends like 3⁵⁷; the cycle of 3 is 3, 9, 7, 1 and 57 mod 4 = 1, so the digit is 3. 17²³ ends like 7²³; the cycle of 7 is 7, 9, 3, 1 and 23 mod 4 = 3, so the digit is 3. The product ends in 3 × 3 = 9.
questions.trap: Using the wrong position in the cycle.
